Who has scored the lowest round in PGA Championship history? Until 2024, nearly 20 golfers shared the tournament's 18-hole scoring record with 63s. But then Xander Schauffele became the first golfer in PGA Championship history to fire a 62.
Schauffele's 9-under par score in the first round of the [2024 PGA Championship](https://www.golfcompendium.com/2022/05/2024-pga-championship.html), played on the par-71 Valhalla Golf Club, was the first 62 in tournament history. Schauffele's round started from the No. 10 tee, so he played the course's back nine first, then finished on the front nine. He had five birdies in his first nine holes (Nos. 11, 13, 15, 16 and 18) for a 31. Then he closed with another 31 with birdies on Nos. 2, 4, 5 and 8.
At the time, Schauffele already shared [the U.S. Open's 18-hole scoring record](https://www.golfcompendium.com/2022/05/18-hole-scoring-record-us-open.html) with a 62. That makes him the first golfer with multiple 62s in majors, and the first golfer to score 62 in two different majors.
It took only two rounds for someone to tie Shauffele, however. In the third round of the 2024 PGA Championship, Shane Lowry became the second golfer with a 62 in this major. Lowry carded a 29 on the front nine of Valhalla, and a 33 on the back nine. Lowry had a putt on the last green of the round for a 61, but just missed.

## Early life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Xander_Schauffele&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]
Schauffele was born on October 25, 1993, in [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego"), California,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-4) to Chen Ping-Yi and Stefan Schauffele.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-5) His mother was born in [Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan "Taiwan"), but grew up in Japan before moving to the United States.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-6) His father Stefan was born in [Stuttgart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuttgart "Stuttgart") to a French-Austrian mother and a German father.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-7) Stefan was an aspiring [decathlete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decathlete "Decathlete"). While traveling to the German national training center at age 20, he was hit by a drunk driver and suffered career-ending injuries.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-9) During recovery, he became interested in golf, and later moved to the United States. He worked at a golf academy in San Diego and as an assistant golf professional in Hawaii.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-:2-10)
Schauffele's parents met at San Diego's [United States International University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_International_University "United States International University") in 1988 and married three months afterwards.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-:0-11) They then moved to Germany, where Xander's elder brother Nico was born, before returning to San Diego.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xander_Schauffele#cite_note-12)
